fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled XML document bytes are extracted from the fuzz input as the main entity.

fine_trace.code: doc = xmlCtxtReadMemory(ctxt, docBuffer, docSize, docUrl, NULL, opts & ~XML_PARSE_DTDVALID);
fine_trace.note: The XML document is parsed without DTD validation so the tree is built for later post-validation.
Post-validation invokes xmlValidateDocument which walks the tree and calls xmlValidateElement on each element.
For each attribute with children, the attribute value is serialized with inLine=0, which sets escape=1 and, since doc->encoding is NULL, sets XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII.
The attribute text node content, containing a non-ASCII byte, is passed to xmlEscapeText with XML_ESCAPE_NON_ASCII set.
The non-ASCII character yields offset<0, so a stack-allocated tempBuf[12] is filled via xmlSerializeHexCharRef and repl points to it; tempBuf goes out of scope at the closing brace of the else block.
memcpy reads replSize bytes from repl, which points to the out-of-scope stack buffer tempBuf, causing a stack-use-after-scope read.
